answer: An economy of AI agents can resist Sybil attacks by implementing verifiable computational stakes, which act as a digital pigment tracing verifiable resource expenditure across nodes. When agents collaborate to reach a network summit, cryptographic zero-knowledge proofs validate unique hardware origins, creating a decentralized gale of verification that strips fraudulent identities of voting weight. The attacker cost scales directly with hardware acquisition, rendering mass-identity forgery economically unfeasible.
